event.summary: Removal of byte-stream fallback is deliberate and protocol-fenced
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: An older page left open across an update can misdraw a terminal and have its input refused until reload; the specification explicitly accepts this transition. Details: the assigned patch removes ViewerStreams, stream_kind, settle_bytes, and send_input and always starts grid flow after Attached (client.rs:4013-4070). Governing SPEC_impl.md, Grid streams (3009-3027), says: 'Protocol 77 removed the byte streams with the old terminals and xterm.js: every attachment’s data channel carries a grid stream' (apostrophe normalized here), and exactly: 'A page loaded from the previous helm and left open across the update must be reloaded; nothing keeps it working.' It also says exactly: 'Keeping the stream notice for such pages was considered and not done: a reload is the whole remedy.' Proposed_drop: explicit specification acceptance of stale-page misdrawing/input refusal, pending independent check; byte-only peer removal also requires source verification of hello mismatch rejection. Suggested bucket: high/material UX for the stale-page effect if it were not accepted. Confidence: confirmed specification acceptance, not runtime-observed. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route; the described malformed-input path ends an attachment, not its agent. possible_cover: none; coverage sources were not consulted. Caveat: this record does not establish the handshake implementation, which remains to be checked in the initial pass.

event.summary: Removal of byte-stream fallback is deliberate and protocol-fenced
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: An older page left open across an update can misdraw a terminal and have its input refused until reload; the specification explicitly accepts this transition. Original consequence preserved: SPEC_impl.md:3023-3027 says that reconnect from the old page, automatic in the build-latch window or manual, draws grid messages as terminal output, and typing ends the attachment as malformed input. Exact acceptance: 'A page loaded from the previous helm and left open across the update must be reloaded; nothing keeps it working.' Exact acceptance: 'Keeping the stream notice for such pages was considered and not done: a reload is the whole remedy.' proposed_drop: explicit specification acceptance of that stale-browser consequence, still proposed; no independent drop accepted. Distinct source-refuted route: a mismatched helm and supervisor cannot negotiate an attachment. farhelm-proto/src/lib.rs:255 sets protocol 77; start_with_seams completes handshake before installing client routing, and proto/io.rs:585-658 accepts only exact equality. This agrees with g053/c1 (browser acceptance) and g053/c2 (peer protocol fence); browser acceptance is not evidence of peer compatibility. Source checks preserved: client.rs:4016-4037 unconditionally installs a grid-sized queue and shared QueueGauge before Attach; 4062-4069 starts helm flow on every accepted reply, unless already released. terminal.rs:762-774 calls send_grid_input and stops reading on refusal; client.rs:4111-4133 removes only the attachment and signals Detach on oversized input. service/handlers.rs:1903-1943 sends Attached before starting GridSender and installs HostAttach input. Synthesis teardown check: handlers.rs:1952-1977 matches channel and owning connection, removes only that attachment and joins its output task; ActiveAttach at service/terminals.rs:417-468 holds the viewer's flow/input pump, not an agent process. HostAttach::drop (service/grid_stream.rs:1169-1175) sends pump cancellation only; GridSender's shutdown returns Requested (937-962). Supervisor stall/natural-detach arbiters also verify channel, connection and forwarder identity before removing only that attachment (service/connection.rs:1427-1517). These paths do not terminate the running terminal host or its agent. Independent upgrade lifetime: terminal-host/SPEC.md:3-6 states that a running terminal host outlives every update of its client, and Change policy:501-523 requires permanent shipped wire behavior and compatibility with every shipped host version. The helm-supervisor protocol 77 is separate from terminal_host::protocol::PROTOCOL_VERSION, which remains 1 (terminal-host/src/protocol.rs:29). hosts/client.rs:128-132 imports that independent constant and 1277-1319 uses it for Host Hello/Welcome. The reviewed commit has no diff under crates/terminal-host. Thus removing viewer negotiation does not authorize changing the running host's protocol or lifetime. The separate deliberate old-tmux retirement consequence remains g053/f1; this candidate does not retract or lower it. Suggested bucket: high/material UX for the accepted stale-browser effect if it were not accepted. Confidence: confirmed source and contract analysis, not observed execution. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route from this stale-browser/attachment behavior; malformed input ends the viewer attachment, not its agent. possible_cover: none; related group records were supplied for interface synthesis, and excluded queue coverage sources were not consulted. Caveats: no tests or reproductions run; helm-supervisor incompatibility blocks host access until matching versions run, while an old browser needs reload. Revision reason: synthesis separated the two version boundaries and validated teardown through the supervisor, preserving the exact old-page consequence and its pending proposed drop.

event.summary: Smaller overflow-test queues retain the intended coverage
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: No user-visible defect established. Considered whether retaining 256-slot synthetic test queues after production moves uniformly to 4096 events masks a missing production admission bound. Details: TEST_EVENT_QUEUE at client.rs:4759-4766 explicitly targets mpsc Full, and register_terminal at 4773-4796 still uses the real QueueGauge. route_terminal_event at 2471-2495 applies gauge admission before try_send, and both refusal paths remove the route and call detach_stalled_terminal. The gauge test at 6409-6523 separately fills GRID_EVENT_QUEUE, refuses its next event, pins the 1 MiB frame and 16 MiB byte bounds, checks pause/resume at both marks, and checks release before delayed flow startup. The accepted-attachment integration test at 6597-6654 exercises flow startup and byte overflow through the real demultiplexer. This split preserves the tested mechanisms: the synthetic capacity tests head-of-line isolation and marker overflow, while the gauge and attach tests pin production accounting. Contract: SPEC_impl.md, Grid streams, 3029-3038, requires at most 4096 frames and 16 MiB, helm-owned pause/resume and no blocking of the shared reader. Suggested bucket: other/test coverage if established. Confidence: confirmed source refutation; no execution performed. proposed_drop: source refutation, no production-bound coverage regression established. Could-be-highest: no; this consideration concerns test mechanism coverage, with no demonstrated shipped security or work-loss route. possible_cover: none. Caveat: source review does not claim these tests were executed or passed.

event.summary: Smaller overflow-test queues retain the intended coverage
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: No user-visible defect established. Original consideration preserved: retaining 256-slot synthetic test queues after production moves uniformly to 4096 events might mask a missing production admission bound. Initial source checks preserved: TEST_EVENT_QUEUE at client.rs:4759-4766 explicitly targets mpsc Full; register_terminal at 4773-4796 still uses the real QueueGauge. route_terminal_event at 2471-2495 applies gauge admission before try_send; both refusal paths remove only that route and call detach_stalled_terminal. The gauge test at 6409-6523 separately fills GRID_EVENT_QUEUE, refuses the next event, pins the 1 MiB frame and 16 MiB byte bounds, checks pause/resume at both marks and release before delayed startup. The accepted-attachment test at 6597-6654 exercises flow startup and byte overflow through the real demultiplexer. Synthesis checks: both public attachment entry points converge on attach_with_policy (3993-4017), which unconditionally creates mpsc::channel(GRID_EVENT_QUEUE), QueueGauge::new and a shared gauge in both the handle and stream (4016-4037); no negotiation-dependent accounting path remains. Every accepted Attached starts grid flow unless the handle was already released (4062-4069 and 866-877), while the gauge admits data from registration onward (837-849). Both recv and try_recv release counted events through taken (931-992). Overflow never awaits queue capacity: try_send removes only the occupied entry, signals its out-of-band detach and spawns release_upstream (2436-2519). This independently owned send may wait for the shared writer without parking the shared reader. Dropping TerminalHandle clears its flow and prevents a late Attached from restarting it (747-752). The supervisor's pause lookup matches channel and owning connection (service/connection.rs:1546-1558), and its Detach checks the same ownership and removes only the matching attachment/forwarder (service/handlers.rs:1952-1977). Contract: SPEC_impl.md, Grid streams, 3029-3038, requires at most 4096 frames and 16 MiB, helm-owned flow control and no blocking of the shared reader. Suggested bucket if established: other/test coverage. Confidence: confirmed source refutation; no execution performed. proposed_drop: source refutation, no production-bound coverage regression established; still proposed, no independent drop accepted. Could-be-highest: no demonstrated shipped security or work-loss route in this test-coverage consideration. possible_cover: none. Caveat: source review does not claim the tests were executed or passed; an upstream Detach uses the shared writer and is not a promise of zero scheduling delay. Revision reason: synthesis verified unconditional production accounting and per-attachment isolation across the client/supervisor boundary, preserving the original consideration and source checks.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: No test-oracle defect established from increasing the pre-Attached oversized-data fixture from 64 KiB to 1 MiB. Considered whether the larger frame or peer shutdown causes an earlier framing/connection failure that can masquerade as the intended per-attachment cap enforcement. Source checks: terminal_data_limit_applies_before_attach_and_accepts_the_limit at client.rs:6281-6406 writes GRID_MAX_MESSAGE + 1 before Attached, explicitly requires the upstream Detach for that exact channel, waits for that observation before the second Attach, and then requires an exactly GRID_MAX_MESSAGE all-y data event from the same client connection. proto/lib.rs:484 and Frame::encode/decode at 626-678 permit frames up to 8 MiB including their five-byte kind/channel overhead, so both fixture data lengths are frame-valid. FrameWriter at proto/io.rs:224-230 writes and flushes each frame in order, and the running client reader routes before reading the later reply. A generic connection failure cannot satisfy the stalled detach plus successful second attach and exact payload assertions. The peer closes after sending the second reply, but TermStream::recv prefers buffered data before its detached reason (client.rs:931-976), preserving the exact-limit observable. Parent-commit comparison confirms this patch changes the cap/stream negotiation rather than inventing the test's sequencing; the test also exists at the range's exclusive base.
